principle: Any market can be learned through the same universal market-learning architecture. Where PirePoint has a dedicated market guide, the routine can connect to verified local material; where it does not, the routine must clearly distinguish universal knowledge from destination-specific verification.
universalModules: What market is this, which venues matter, who regulates it, what securities are actually being studied?
How an investor reaches the market, account/custody requirements, foreign access and practical friction.
Exchanges, venues, listing segments, ownership forms, participants and price formation.
Share classes, ETFs/funds, derivatives, ADR/GDR-style instruments where relevant, dividends, splits and other actions.
Sessions, auctions, order types, shorting, clearing, custody, settlement and operational mechanics.
Regulators, rulebooks, disclosure obligations, enforcement and investor protections.
Fiscal year, filing cadence, accounting standards, presentation, segment reporting and comparability traps.
Founders/promoters, state ownership, institutions, voting, related parties, boards and shareholder rights.
FX, monetary policy, inflation, fiscal conditions and how macro variables reach sectors and earnings.
Which industries matter, local economics, industry structure, regulation and business-model differences.
Where primary evidence lives, issuer disclosures, exchange data, regulator material and source hierarchy.
Earnings quality, multiples, cash flows, rates, currency, sector mix, expectations and cross-market comparability.
Liquidity, currency, governance, regulation, concentration, political/legal, accounting and operational risks.
Take a real company through business, financials, cash, capital allocation, valuation, risks and evidence.
Prove what transferred, identify misleading assumptions and stress-test the learner in unfamiliar cases.

learningPath.principle: 300 learning nodes are available; the learner does not have to answer 300 questions. Nodes are taught, tested, researched or revisited according to evidence.

nodes.title: Market identity — foundation
nodes.objective: Learn market identity for India: What the market is, why it exists, its economic role, major venues and the map of institutions. Apply it to a real India market/company context, identify what is local rather than assumed, and verify important claims against the appropriate primary source.
nodes.learn: Understand the concept, explain the mechanism, identify the India-specific rule or convention, apply it to a real example, and test where the familiar assumption from another market breaks.

learningArchitecture.rule: Every dedicated market has a 300-node learning map. The 300 nodes cover foundations, local market mechanics, company analysis, research, valuation, risk, comparison and mastery. The route is adaptive: users see only what is useful now, while the complete map remains inspectable.
learningArchitecture.note: A node is not merely a title. It has an objective, learning action, proof type, destination-market context and primary-source checkpoints. Market-specific guides should progressively replace generic objectives with fully authored local lessons.
